transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-22
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE); Ravi Patel (Borealis CTO); Sophie Gomez (Head of ML); Evan Brooks (Infra Eng); Dina Lopez (Product)

Summary:
Quick scoping for the POC runway: define kickoff, access gates, mid-point review, exec readout criteria and benchmarks. Focus on workload sizing (chat vs long-runner vs embeddings), network access (VPC peering / temporary keys), and success/decision gates (latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, quality metrics).

Topics covered:
- POC timeline and concrete milestones
- Access and networking constraints (VPC, IP allowlist, KMS)
- Benchmark plan (datasets, metrics, target SLOs)
- Success criteria and exec readout framing

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call and we'll jump into the runway and gate definitions.
[00:35] Ravi (Borealis CTO): hey, thanks. real quick context, we're evaluating a hosted-first approach but need the option to move to private or dedicated for some high-security workloads. timeline is tight — exec wants an initial readout in 8 weeks.
[01:10] Liam (Redwood SE): got it. advisable to break the POC into kickoff, access + baseline, midpoint benchmark, and exec readout. we typically do a 6–8 week runway for the full readout; with early fail/pass gates at weeks 2 and 4.
[01:45] Sophie (Head of ML): for our side success means: p95 latency under 300ms for short conversational flows, throughput >200 req/s for our peak, and embeddings within 50ms for single vector ops. also quality checks: rouge/emd-ish measures and human review on 200 samples.
[02:20] Dina (Product): plus the business metric — latency at scale must not push down engagement by >5%.
[02:50] Maya: that's helpful — we'll map those into decision gates. high-level milestone plan i want us to agree on: kickoff this week, access + baseline (1 week), run benchmark sprint (2 weeks), mid-point readout (week 3), remediation/optimizations (weeks 4–5), exec readout (week 8).
[03:30] Evan (Infra): on access we have strict egress policies. we prefer VPC peering and temporary NAT paths; not comfortable with open internet keys. can you support a VPC private deployment or peering?
[04:00] Liam: yes we support VPC peering for Redwood Private; for hosted we can do secure peering and token scoping. we'll give a small test window for quick perf tests. the SE team will provide a lightweight harness that can run inside your VPC to avoid egress.
[04:40] Ravi: what about encryption and KMS? we need CMK integration and audit logs for token usage.
[05:05] Maya: we have KMS integrations in private deployments and audit logs in Dedicated/Private. i'll include the security pack in the SOW.
[05:35] Sophie: for benchmarks: we'll need three workload profiles — chat(2–5 turns, avg 32 tokens), long generation (~512 tokens), embeddings (single query). can you size required GPU capacity?
[06:10] Liam: yes. initial sizing estimate: for chat at our target throughput, 2x A100 equivalent or a few instance types. but we'll provide a more precise load map after we see the prompt set and token histograms. we also suggested testing a quantized 13B variant vs 70B float to evaluate cost vs quality.
[06:55] Dina: timeline question — how long for the Redwood team to set the harness and run baseline?
[07:10] Liam: we can supply the harness within 2 business days of prompts. baseline run (cold-cache p95, warm-cache, throughput with batching) takes ~48 hours to run and analyze.
[07:35] Maya: so practical milestone dates: kickoff week of 2026-12-28, baseline complete by 2027-01-03, midpoint review around 2027-01-12, exec readout first week of February. does that align?
[08:05] Ravi: yes, that works with our exec calendar.
[08:25] Sophie: on success criteria please include both SLOs and quality thresholds — e.g., automated similarity metrics plus panel review where 85% of outputs are acceptable.
[08:50] Liam: agreed. we'll propose automatic metrics: p95 latency, avg tokens-per-second, cost per 1k tokens, and a quality delta relative to your current baseline. for human eval we'll do 200 sampled prompts, blind review.
[09:20] Evan: do you have templates for the VPC peering change? we'll need IP ranges, ports, and timing windows.
[09:40] Maya: yes — i'll attach a networking checklist and a short runbook for peering in the follow-up.
[09:55] Ravi: curious about fallbacks — if hosted capacity is constrained, can you route to a smaller quantized model automatically?
[10:20] Liam: yes, smart routing is available; in the POC we can configure fallbacks to lower-cost variants and measure quality impact. that's part of the optimization sprint.
[10:40] Dina: cost targets — we want to understand unit cost at expected volume. what's realistic?
[11:00] Liam: initial roughs: quantized 13B can reduce token cost by ~3–5x versus 70B fp16 depending on prompt length; we'll model cost per 1k tokens in the benchmark report.
[11:35] Sophie: for the mid-point review, what deliverables should we expect?
[11:50] Maya: mid-point will include: baseline metrics, quality samples, a list of tuning/ops items, and a recommendation (pass / remediation / escalate). exec readout will include a short slide deck and an ops runbook for handover.
[12:20] Ravi: what's the pass/fail bar at mid-point?
[12:35] Liam: typically: if we hit >80% of throughput/latency targets and quality is within your acceptance threshold (say ≤15% regression), we mark pass. otherwise remediation. final exec decision at week 8.
[13:05] Sophie: are there any tricky gotchas we've seen with customers similar to us?
[13:20] Liam: yes — common items: tokenization surprises (longer token counts than expected), KV cache warm-up affecting initial latencies, and network NAT limits. we'll include tests that surface those.
[13:50] Maya: okay i'm going to summarize the concrete gates in the SOW: Gate 1 (access + baseline): infrastructure and credentials validated; Gate 2 (midpoint): metrics and sample quality; Gate 3 (exec): recommendation and go/no-go.
[14:20] Dina: on personnel — who should attend midpoint and exec readout? exec readout needs CTO + Head of Product + VP Eng. midpoint can be hands-on ML + infra + product.
[14:45] Maya: noted. matchmaking will be in the SOW.
[15:00] Ravi: timeline risks? holiday season might slow approvals.
[15:15] Maya: yes, we'll build buffer days — the 8-week target is soft if approvals slip.
[15:40] Sophie: about the benchmark harness — does it include replaying real traffic shape?
[15:55] Liam: we'll provide a replay harness; we ask for sample trace/traffic profile. if that's sensitive, you can run the harness internally and share metrics.
[16:20] Evan: can we get a small throughput test inside our VPC before opening full access?
[16:35] Liam: yes, we'll set up a limited window and a minimal-access agent. we'll coordinate the port/IPs.
[17:00] Maya: next steps — i'll send SOW, Liam will send harness and sample prompt template, Evan will share peering contact and window.
[17:20] Dina: can we get the proposed mid-point agenda?
[17:35] Maya: yes — baseline summary, anomaly review, ops checklist, final recommendations — i'll include that in the follow-up.
[18:00] Ravi: great. any other concerns?
[18:10] Sophie: one more — human eval logistics. we'll need Redwood to anonymize outputs and give scoring rubric.
[18:25] Liam: we'll provide anonymization steps and a Google sheet rubric for your reviewers.
[18:40] Maya: alright wrapping up — i'll follow-up with the SOW and networking runbook today. Liam will aim to provide harness by 12/29.
[19:00] Ravi: thanks everyone — looking forward.

(There are intermittent short cross-talks and small disfluencies; transcription not perfect — some product names occasionally mis-transcribed.)
